title: Signal-Adjusted Opportunity Funnel (SAOF) for Capacity-Constrained Roadmaps
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Problem: Current RICE-derived prioritization produces noisy rankings when token cost and latency interact nonlinearly across workloads and capacity tiers. We frequently see features score highly on reach/impact but become impractical under Dedicated/Private capacity constraints or when autoscale policies trigger costly bursts. Goal: Design and prototype a lightweight prioritization layer — the Signal-Adjusted Opportunity Funnel (SAOF) — that adjusts RICE-like scores using workload signals (token-velocity cohorts, latency-sensitive fraction, peak:baseline ratio) and capacity regime multipliers (hosted vs dedicated vs private) to surface initiatives that are deployable and cost-effective across our three deployment modes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented SAOF formula and rubric that maps input signals to an adjusted priority score (human-readable, reproducible).
2) A reference spreadsheet with example initiatives (n>=12) showing both raw RICE and SAOF-adjusted rankings and delta explanations.
3) A short simulation (CSV) that applies SAOF to historical usage slices and demonstrates reduced regret for top-3 picks under capacity constraints.
4) PM/Eng/Design sign-off on rubric and rollout approach.
5) Playbook page added to Confluence with usage guidance and an example prioritization workflow.
notes_and_decisions:
- 2026-01-15 decision: use token-velocity cohorts (low/med/high) and latency-sensitivity buckets (best-effort / interactive / synchronous) as primary signals.
- 2026-01-20 tradeoff: heavier weighting on capacity multipliers increases stability of top picks but may hide high-impact speculative bets; we will surface suppressed high-impact items in a "speculative" view rather than top funnel.
- 2026-01-28 alignment: UX will show both raw RICE and SAOF-adjusted score with a short explanation for transparency.
- 2026-02-10 change: add a 'fallback-upgrade' tag for initiatives that become viable with a modest Dedicated reserve (to help sales/finance conversations).

implementation_notes: Prototype phase: spreadsheet + simulation. If prototype delta is promising (>15% reduction in regret on historical slices), engineer a small helper service to compute SAOF scores for quarterly roadmap exports (API + CSV). Implementation scope and effort to be re-estimated at that time.
risks: 1) Overfitting to historical workload patterns that change post-launch. 2) Perceived loss of transparency if adjustments aren't explainable. 3) Upstream data quality gaps (cohort extraction, route tagging) could bias outcomes.

estimated_business_outcome: Reduce priority-selection regret for capacity-constrained quarters by >=15%, and provide a transparent mechanism to surface speculative/transformational bets separately. This should improve roadmap deployability and reduce last-minute scope reshuffles tied to Dedicated capacity limits.
notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing the rubric, please: (a) check that capacity multipliers reflect realistic Dedicated reservation thresholds; (b) flag any signals we are missing (eg. legal/regulatory runway for Private deployments); (c) confirm the behavioral guidance for when to surface suppressed speculative items.
historical_context: This ticket grows from PM-314271 (scope prioritization pilot) and recurrent feedback from Eng SRE and Sales about feature de-prioritization late in the cycle due to capacity/cost mismatches. Prior attempts leaned on raw RICE and ad-hoc filters; SAOF aims to formalize the filter into a score adjustment rather than a hard cutoff.
